title: Machine learning identifies covalent organic frameworks for hydrogen peroxide photosynthesis
summary: An ensemble machine-learning framework combined data augmentation, multilevel structural descriptors and physics-informed features to screen more than 10,000 covalent organic framework candidates. The researchers synthesized and tested eight selected COFs. The paper reports COF-343 at 12,978.7 μmol H2O2 h−1 g−1, with additional measured results for COF-2449, COF-2835 and COF-8484. This is one study-level materials result, not four discoveries. Detailed standard-test conditions in the supplement were not reviewed, and the results do not establish industrial performance. A data/code deposit may predate the journal article, but its date and result content were not checked here.
ai_technology: Deep neural network ensemble; random-forest band-position model

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Synthesis article page, abstract, methods/results text and author metadata as indexed by publisher.

evidence.tested: The indexed primary article reports synthesis and photocatalytic testing of eight selected COFs, including measured H2O2 production rates for COF-343, COF-2449, COF-2835 and COF-8484.
evidence.unknown: Detailed standard-test conditions in the supplementary information were not reviewed; the reported laboratory rates do not establish industrial performance. Zenodo deposit chronology/content was not checked.
evidence.ai_role: A DNN ensemble predicted photocatalytic yields and a random-forest model estimated band positions to guide COF screening.
